candidates.title: cartesi.tojson with an indent above 512 reads past the end of nlohmann's indentation buffer: it copies heap bytes into the JSON text, and a larger indent crashes the process
candidates.component: Lua JSON bindings (cartesi.tojson -> clua_tojson -> nlohmann::json::dump(indent)), vendored nlohmann-json 3.12.0 serializer
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'the Lua helper libraries (... the JSON bindings)'). As a library, it stands in for the most critical role among the components that reach the defect through it. Every in-tree caller passes a constant indent of -1 or 2 (cartesi-machine.lua, hash-tree.lua frontier store, prt.lua epoch state, cartesi-rollup-data.lua), and none of those values triggers it.
candidates.location: third-party/nlohmann-json/json.hpp serializer::dump, lines 18849-18853 (object), 18922-18926 and 18983-18987 (arrays): 'if (indent_string.size() < new_indent) indent_string.resize(indent_string.size() * 2, ' ');' followed by 'o->write_characters(indent_string.c_str(), new_indent)'. indent_string starts at 512 bytes (line 18795) and is doubled only once per level. Reached from src/clua-cartesi.cpp cartesi_mod_tojson (indent = clua_opt_integer<int>(L, 2, -1), any int is accepted) -> src/clua-i-machine.cpp clua_tojson line 748 's = j.dump(indent)'.
candidates.description: nlohmann's pretty-printer grows its indentation buffer by doubling it once whenever the buffer is shorter than the new indentation. It then copies new_indent bytes from the buffer. When one indentation step is larger than the current buffer size (the buffer starts at 512, so any indent above 512 on the first nested level, and above 1024 after one doubling), the copy reads past the end of the heap buffer. cartesi.tojson passes the caller's integer indent to dump() unchecked. Any indent in 513..INT_MAX on a value with at least one nested container is enough. The out-of-bounds heap bytes go into the returned Lua string, which is an information leak into data the caller may write to files or send over the network. A large enough indent faults on an unmapped page and kills the Lua process with SIGSEGV. The C API and the JSON-RPC server always dump with -1, so they are not affected.
candidates.trigger: A trusted Lua caller of cartesi.tojson(value, indent, ...) with indent > 512 and a nested value. No in-tree code path derives the indent from data from other parties. Every caller uses a constant -1 or 2.
candidates.reachability: Not reachable from data from other parties in any in-tree component. The indent comes from the caller's code, never from input payloads, logs, proofs or player messages. The defect is a host-side memory-safety bug in a Lua helper library, not a state of the machine.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? Section 8 excludes 'Defects that need an untrusted party to call the machine API directly'. Here the caller is trusted, so that exclusion does not apply directly. The trigger is a caller-chosen parameter, not data from other parties. 2 Role: Support. AUDIT.md lists 'the Lua helper libraries (... the JSON bindings)' as Support, and section 3 says 'A library stands in for the most critical role among the components that reach the defect through it'. No component reaches it with a triggering indent. 3 High/Medium cases: Medium applies to 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium', which needs the defect to rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for. Section 4 requires memory safety on 'Every path that carries such data' (data from other parties), and the indent is not such data. So the Critical entry 'Memory corruption or code execution through data from other parties that the honest operator must process' and the High entry 'A crash, hang, memory-safety defect ... caused by data from other parties that the honest operator may decline' do not apply. 4 Critical: no rule is violated at a reachable state or on the honest operator's path. 5 Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model ... Examples are ... a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller'. Arguably not even misuse, because the API documents and accepts any int indent, but either way it is Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: No direct threat to the section 1 goal. It is a latent memory-safety defect (heap over-read with an information leak, and a crash) in a binding that the PRT tooling uses to persist state (prt.lua epoch state, hash-tree frontiers). If any future caller computes the indent from configuration or relayed data, it becomes a crash or leak in support or operator tooling.
candidates.evidence: Found by my Lua-binding fuzzer under the ASan+UBSan build (seed 1, about 850 calls). ASan reported 'heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 1100' in memcpy <- basic_string::append <- nlohmann output_string_adapter::write_characters <- serializer::dump (json.hpp:18859) <- cartesi::clua_tojson (clua-i-machine.cpp:748) <- cartesi_mod_tojson. Minimal reproducer /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/DYNAPI/repro-indent.lua: cartesi.tojson({{1}}, N). On the plain (non-sanitized) in-tree build: N=600 gives a clean result. N=1100 returns 4409 bytes, 89 of which are not spaces or JSON structure (leaked heap bytes). N=5000 returns 20009 bytes, 13611 of them leaked. N=100000 and N=10000000 make lua5.4 die with SIGSEGV (rc 139). Under ASan, N=1100 aborts with the heap-buffer-overflow report.
candidates.test_idea: In Lua with the in-tree module: local s = cartesi.tojson({{1}}, 5000), then assert that s consists only of spaces, newlines and the characters of '[[1]]' (or that the call raises a clean 'indent out of range' error). A fixed build must either reject indents above a bound or grow indent_string to at least new_indent (for example resize(max(size*2, new_indent))). Run the call in a child process so that a SIGSEGV also counts as a failure (exit 1).

not_covered: Exactly what I ran: (a) JSON-RPC wire fuzzer (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/DYNAPI/rpcfuzz.py) against the ASan+UBSan cartesi-jsonrpc-machine, with allocator_may_return_null=1: 4486 requests over 4 seeds (300, 1490, 1809, 887). It covered all 46 machine.* and top-level methods except fork, rebind, shutdown, emancipate, delay_next_request, load, store, clone_stored, rename_stored, remove_stored and sync_stored. Parameter mutations covered integer edges (2^31, 2^32, 2^53, 2^63, 2^64 and negatives), floats, invalid base64, wrong types, dropped and extra fields, object and array forms, and mutated real logs for verify_step_uarch, verify_reset_uarch and verify_send_cmio_response. About 8% of requests were raw byte mutations: truncation, byte flips, nesting of 255 to 100000 levels, batches of up to 50 requests, hostile ids. Results: no ASan or UBSan memory or UB report. Three server aborts were ASan out-of-memory on caller-chosen machine.read_console_output max_length (2^35-1 and 2^63-1) in std::vector(max_length); these are ASan-only allocator aborts on a trusted parameter, not reported. One 20-second timeout was read_virtual_memory of 2 GiB (caller-chosen). (b) Lua-binding fuzzer (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/DYNAPI/luafuzz.lua), in-process under ASan: about 2400 calls over seeds 1 to 5, covering every machine method except store, load, create, destroy and the stored-directory functions, plus cartesi.tojson, fromjson, frombase64, fromhex, keccak256 and sha256. It found the tojson indent over-read (candidate 1). It also hit collect_mcycle_bundle(0,2,32) reserving 2^32 hashes (128 GiB), an ASan OOM that is a documented eager reservation on a trusted parameter, not reported. Other stops were caller-chosen long runs (run to 2^53 mcycles, run(nil) on a guest my fuzzer had corrupted). (c) Differential local-versus-JSON-RPC fuzzer (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/DYNAPI/difffuzz.lua): about 130 completed cases (seed 2) plus an unknown number in the timed-out seed 1, with mutated verify_* logs and hostile send_cmio_response/log_send_cmio_response data, reasons, revert hashes and log types. It compared accept/reject, after-hashes, returned logs and machine root hashes, and found zero divergences. (d) Hand probes: Lua numbers at 2^53, 2^63 and 2^64, NaN and inf into integer parameters (all clean errors). fromjson/tojson with hostile user schema dictionaries (cycles, non-string types, tuple length mismatch, ArrayIndex at INT64 limits: all clean errors, no ASan report). Total compute was about 25 CPU-minutes, single-threaded per process, somewhat above the 20-minute guideline because the ASan JSON-RPC runs were slow.

The JSON-RPC volume is small (4486 requests, under 1500 of them on the verify_* and cmio methods). The differential local-versus-remote run is very small (about 130 cases): ASan made remote calls carrying MiB-sized base64 data too slow for the budget.

Methods with side effects outside the scratch directory: fork, rebind, shutdown, emancipate, machine.load/store/clone_stored/rename_stored/remove_stored/sync_stored with hostile paths and directories, and machine.create/replace_memory_range with mutated configurations (only lightly mutated through the template).

The C API (cm.h) was not driven by a native C harness. Null pointers and length/buffer mismatches were only read in cm.cpp (cm_send_cmio_response relies on machine::send_cmio_response's null check; cm_receive_cmio_request and cm_read_console_output trust the caller's lengths). Its JSON inputs go through the same json-util parsers that the JSON-RPC fuzz exercised.
Binary main-processor step logs (cm_verify_step / machine.verify_step) under adversarial page contents with a consistent root: not fuzzed (ZK-related).
The JSON-RPC client (libcartesi_jsonrpc) parsing hostile server replies (the server is trusted), and fork_server/rebind failure paths.
Uninstrumented production behavior of very large caller-chosen allocations (read_console_output vector(max_length), collect_*_bundle reserve) under vm.overcommit settings: not measured.
Lua luaL_error longjmp across C++ frames (leaks only) and the known sparse-table loop in clua_get_array_table_len under a schema: not re-examined.
cartesi.hash-tree.lua frontier and forest functions and the PRT recipes' own decoding of player messages (game-transport/prtu) were not fuzzed.
